citation: C. Mead, L. Conway, "Introduction to VLSI Systems", Addison-Wesley, 1980.
title: Introduction to VLSI Systems
authors: Carver A. Mead; Lynn A. Conway

segments.title: Front matter
segments.why: The front matter provides publication context and a general VLSI motivation without arithmetic-unit design detail.

segments.title: MOS Devices and Circuits
segments.why: The chapter covers general MOS devices, logic circuits, delay, and scaling rather than an arithmetic-unit mechanism.

segments.title: Integrated System Fabrication
segments.why: The chapter concerns fabrication processes, design rules, yield, and conductor limits rather than arithmetic-unit architecture.

segments.title: Data and Control Flow in Systematic Structures
segments.why: The chapter presents general data/control structures, registers, programmable logic, and finite-state machines without a covered arithmetic-unit mechanism.

segments.title: Implementing Integrated System Designs
segments.why: The chapter covers layout, fabrication, design tools, simulation, and testing rather than arithmetic-unit mechanisms.

segments.title: Architecture and Design of a Data Processing Engine
segments.why: The chapter gives implementation detail for a 16-bit arithmetic logic unit and barrel shifter, which can inform its carry-propagating adder and mux-tree shifter families.
